title: Federated Single Sign-On and Zero Trust Co-design for AI and HPC Digital Research Infrastructures
problem: Scientific workflows spanning distributed HPC, AI, ML, and edge computing systems require secure identity and access management across heterogeneous platforms. The technical challenge is implementing strong security controls, compliance requirements, and multi-factor authentication while maintaining seamless federated single sign-on.
motivation: Scientific productivity demands balancing robust cybersecurity and regulatory compliance with user accessibility across heterogeneous distributed computing resources.
method: The system uses federated identity management—where users log in once through their home institution and access multiple systems without separate passwords—combined with zero-trust security (verifying every user and access request, not trusting by default). It enforces multiple verification layers: multi-factor authentication (passwords plus a second factor like a phone code), cloud-native protocols (industry-standard secure login methods), and time-limited role-based access that automatically expires. The system monitors all access attempts, alerts administrators to suspicious activity, and ensures compliance with security regulations, deployed on Isambard-AI and HPC supercomputing facilities in the UK.
key_novelty: The key idea is co-designing federated single sign-on (one login across multiple systems) and zero-trust security (verify all access rather than assuming trust) together as an integrated system for scientific computing that combines HPC and AI infrastructure.
contributions: Implementation of federated IAM with zero-trust security principles and multi-factor authentication
Integration of time-limited RBAC with cloud-native protocols for compliance
Deployment architecture on national research infrastructure with monitoring and alerting frameworks
User workflow demonstrations for different roles across HPC and AI systems
limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Federated identity and access management for scientific computing
